Subject: DPA / SCCs - transfer impact and evidence request

Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal here at BlueLine asked us to confirm a few things before we can complete procurement: specifically the DPA language around international transfers, the proposed SCC baseline, and a short list of operational evidence (KMS, subprocessor roster, SOC2).

I attached the DPA your team shared and flagged the clauses we'd like clarified. Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will accept the standard EU Commission SCCs (controller->processor) with your proposed processor/processor roles mapped in an addendum,
- If a transfer-impact addendum is available (we want to avoid a full TIA if possible), and
- Estimated timing to get a clean redline back so our legal can provision a PO.

We're targeting an internal signoff by Friday if possible.

Best,
Oliver
BlueLine Therapeutics

Attachments: BlueLine_DPA_v1.pdf
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs - transfer impact and evidence request

Thanks Oliver — appreciate the clear ask. Looping Legal (Laura) and Sales Ops (Ben) so we can get a coordinated response and an estimated turnaround. Short answers up front:

- Redwood accepts the EU Commission SCCs; we typically use the controller->processor modular clauses with a supplemental transfer-impact addendum when customers request more details on routing and subprocessors.
- We can prepare a concise transfer-impact addendum (TI-Addendum) scoped to BlueLine's regions and expected data flows — that avoids a lengthy TIA in most cases.
- Target for a redline + TI-Addendum draft from Legal: 48 business hours once we have confirmation on the subprocessor list you expect to use and any non-standard data residency asks.

Laura — can you confirm you'll take the lead on the redline and TI-Addendum? Ben / Karthik — FYI on timing and any commercial gating items we should surface.

Action items for BlueLine: please confirm the approximate list of third-party integrations and whether you require customer-managed KMS or are comfortable with Redwood-managed keys (we support both, with KMS integration details attached).

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: DPA / SCCs - transfer impact and evidence request

Sergio / team — taking point on the legal redline and TI-Addendum. Quick summary of proposed redlines and practical asks so Sales has a single list to share with the customer: 

1) SCCs: we accept the modular SCCs but need the Order Form to list Base Processor/Controller roles and the country routing. We'll add an explicit exhibit mapping processor subprocessors and categories of data.

2) Transfer-impact addendum (TI-Addendum): we'll draft a focused TI-Addendum (2–3 pages) that documents:
   - the legal basis for transfers under SCCs + appropriate technical/organizational safeguards;
   - the regions where data may be processed and fallback routing;
   - a short subprocessor escalation / approval path.

3) Evidence list (to attach to the Order Form or a secure workspace):
   - SOC 2 Type II report (latest 12 months) — redacted OK
   - Subprocessor roster + subprocessors' countries
   - KMS architecture note (customer-managed vs. Redwood-managed)
   - Data retention schedule and deletion flow for ephemeral caches

4) Roles: ask BlueLine to confirm whether they consider Redwood a processor or co-processor for the processed dataset in scope (this affects a small number of clause choices).

5) Exceptions log: if BlueLine needs data locality guarantees for specific datasets, we'll add a limited carve-out in the Order Form (execution dependent, may be a paid add-on).

I'll return a redline and a TI-Addendum draft by end of day Thursday (48 business hours as discussed) assuming they provide the subprocessor list and KMS preference by EOD Wednesday.

I'll attach the redline as a Word doc (Redlines_Sergio_Legal_v1.docx). Please let me know if Sales needs talking points for procurement.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
